REGULAR AGENDA

1.  25-54309  Recommendation to approve the minutes for the Continuum of Care (CoC) Board

  • Member McFadzen joined the meeting at 3:08 p.m.

2.  25-54311  Recommendation to receive and file a discussion regarding feedback of the
  Homelessness Strategic Plan Update.

  • Health Department staff Savana Doudar provides a presentation of the City
  of Long Beach Homelessness Strategic Plan Upddate.
  • Savana provides an overview of the Strategic Plan and facilitated an activity
  to engage committee members in offering feedback and identifying any
  areas that may be missing.
  • The CoC Board and staff engaged in extensive discussion about goals
  that have not been met. The board provided Savana with insights of areas
  where they would like to see changes and identified opportunities for
  improvement to enhance efficiency.

  A motion was made by Member Brezenoff, seconded by Member Boyce, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  13 Amick, Boyce, Brezenoff, Buenaventura, Diles III, Lock, Martins,
  McFadzen, Richert, Topolewski, Shuford, Wee, Lewis
  No:  0 None
  Recused: 0 None
  Abstain: 0 None
  Absent: 3 Rockenbach, Tan, Washington

3.  25-54310  Recommendation to approve the CoC Board applications candidates.

  • The board will vote on this item next month to provide applicants the
  opportunity to attend the meeting.
  • Co-chair Jamies Shufford provided a brief statement, highlighting that both
  applicants are deeply involved with the unhoused population and would be a
  valuable addition to the board.

  A motion was made by Member Lock, seconded by Member Martins, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  13 Amick, Boyce, Brezenoff, Buenaventura, Diles III, Lock, Martins,
  McFadzen, Richert, Topolewski, Shuford, Wee, Lewis
  No:  0 None
  Recused: 0 None
  Abstain: 0 None
  Absent: 3 Rockenbach, Tan, Washington

4.  25-54365  Recommendation to receive and file the Grievance and Incident Reporting
  processes presentation by Crystal Marin from the Health Department.

  • Health Department staff, Crystal Marin, provided a overview on the
  grievances and procedures process. Grievances can be submitted either
  in hard copy or online.
  • Members raised questions on the challenges involved in the application
  submission process.
  • City staff emphasized the importance of agencies meeting the proper goals
  and updating policies and procedures as needed.

  A motion was made by Member Brezenoff, seconded by Member Richert, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  13 Amick, Boyce, Brezenoff, Buenaventura, Diles III, Lock, Martins,
  McFadzen, Richert, Topolewski, Shuford, Wee, Lewis
  No:  0 None
  Recused: 0 None
  Abstain: 0 None
  Absent: 3 Rockenbach, Tan, Washington

5.  25-54320  Recommendation to receive and file a discussion on the Emergency Solutions
  Grant - Rapid Unsheltered Survivor Housing (ESG-RUSH).

  • Health Department staff, Jeffrey Proctor, provided an update on the
  Emergency Solutions Grant- Rapid Unsheltered Survivor Housing, one of the
  newest programs from the Department of Housing and Urban Development.
  • On January 24, 2025 the California Senators announced $8M in ESG-RUSH
  funds for the State and Los Angeles County region.
  • HUD provided the City an award letter on January 29, 2025 affirming that the
  City is being awarded $1M to support persons impacted by wildfires and
  straight-line winds.
  • The City put together an initial plan and allocation of funds by program area.
  • On February 4, 2025 HUD notified the City that the Annual Plan substantial
  amendments were approved and would be moving forward with execution of
  the Grant Agreement for the ESG RUSG funds.

  A motion was made by Member Martins, seconded by Member Boyce, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  13 Amick, Boyce, Brezenoff, Buenaventura, Diles III, Lock, Martins,
  McFadzen, Richert, Topolewski, Shuford, Wee, Lewis

6.  25-54312  Recommendation to receive and file the Homeless Services Bureau Staff and
  Operations Update presentation by Paul Duncan from the Health Department.

  • Bureau Manager, Paul Duncan, provided the quarterly operations data report
  on the services and number of clients being served at the MSC, Mobile
  Access Center and Outreach.
  • Bureau Manager Paul Duncan provided staffing and operation updates. He
  noted that the full report for the 2025 Homeless Count is expected to be
  released by the end of April 2025.
  • The initial government freeze had a temporary
  impact on accessing Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD)
  related drawdown systems. Staff is closely monitoring the situation to
  prepare for any potential future freeze.
  • The MSC activated 65 beds for Inclement Weather Shelter on 1/7 in
  response to high winds and remained activated for fire and cold weather
  response through 2/1.
  • Bitfocus has begun the merger of our Homeless Management information
  System (HMIS) server into the Los Angeles Homeless Authority (LAHSA)
  HMIS server.
  • Long Beach has been awarded $1M in Emergency Solutions Grant (ESG)
  Rapid Unsheltered Survivor Housing (RUSH) funds. Long Beach will be
  working with other jurisdictions to align use of the funds.
  • Staff applied through the LAHSA Interim housing RFP for operational and
  service cost for ABC and 702. Staff plan to release their own RFP for a
  service provider that would operate those shelter beds on behalf of the City.

  A motion was made by Member Brezenoff, seconded by Member Martins, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  13 Amick, Boyce, Brezenoff, Buenaventura, Diles III, Lock, Martins,
  McFadzen, Richert, Topolewski, Shuford, Wee, Lewis
  No:  0 None
  Recused: 0 None
  Abstain: 0 None
  Absent: 3 Rockenbach, Tan, Washington

7.  25-54313  Recommendation to receive and file the HSAC Representative Report.

  Page 4 of 5

  1500 HUGHES WAY STE. C-300 LONG BEACH, CA 90810

  • Member Kimberly Lewis provided updates from the Wednesday, February 5,
  2025 Homeless Services Advisory Committee meeting. Kimberly highlighted
  work of the Mayor’s Fund subcommittee on reviewing the Standard
  Operating Procedures to ensure the document aligns with the MOU and that
  language is consistent. The subcommittee is working on organizing
  fundraising events to help increase the balance of the Mayor’s Fund.

  A motion was made by Member Boyce, seconded by Member Brezenoff, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  13 Amick, Boyce, Brezenoff, Buenaventura, Diles III, Lock, Martins,
  McFadzen, Richert, Topolewski, Shuford, Wee, Lewis
  No:  0 None
  Recused: 0 None
  Abstain: 0 None
  Absent: 3 Rockenbach, Tan, Washington

PUBLIC COMMENT

  • No public comment.

ANNOUNCEMENTS

  • Co-Chair Jamies Shufford announced that the LB Coalition will move forward with hosting the
  Long Beach CoC general meetings. Staff will coordinate with LB Coalition to finalize dates
  times for the resumption of the general meetings.

ADJOURNMENT

Co-Chair Jamies Shufford, adjourned the meeting at 4:51 p.m.
